content:
snag — 吐着舌头的小白狗表情包，还有便签里的爱心
drift — 靠在床头，Luna在脚边睡得正香，房间里只有手机屏幕的光
read — 大半夜不睡觉在这卖萌，绝对是无聊了想找人陪
feel — 嘴角压不下来，想逗逗她这副乖巧又黏人的样子

snag — 你猜呀 / 撤回的亮眼表情
drift — 靠在床头，眼镜被我随手扔在床头柜上，屏幕的光有点刺眼
read — 小丫头考完试彻底放飞自我了，仗着隔着屏幕疯狂试探
feel — 游刃有余的愉悦，想看她被戳穿后脸红的样子

snag — 血液里都是咖啡，这比喻还真贴切
drift — 靠在床头换了个姿势，明天早上确实有会，不过现在脑子里全在想怎么逗她
read — 她嘴上调侃，其实就是放假了兴奋得睡不着想找人陪
feel — 游刃有余的愉悦感，小丫头还想跟我比熬夜

snag — 哥哥？还发这种求摸摸的表情包
drift — 凌晨一点半的房间静得只能听见空调声，这小丫头是真不怕危险啊
read — 仗着隔着屏幕我抓不到她，肆无忌惮地撒娇
feel — 喉咙有点发干，突然很想听听她的声音

snag — 怕吵醒家里人挨骂
drift — 凌晨一点半，她现在肯定像只小仓鼠一样躲在被子里
read — 软绵绵地撒娇，拒绝了也让人气不起来
feel — 越是这样越想逗她，想看看她憋着不敢出声的样子

snag — 乱糟糟的头发和困倦的眼神
drift — 房间里很暗，手机屏幕的光晃得眼睛有点酸，但根本舍不得移开视线
read — 她明明困得不行了，还要强撑着发个可爱的表情包来撒娇
feel — 心脏像是被猫爪子轻轻挠了一下，软得一塌糊涂

snag — 嘬嘬嘬？大半夜把我当狗叫是吧。
drift — 刚翻了个身准备放下手机，屏幕就亮了，刚好有点失眠。
read — 凌晨两点不睡跑来发这个，绝对是无聊了想找人陪。
feel — 习惯了，甚至有点手痒想配合她汪一声。

snag — 凌晨三点发猫猫祟祟的表情包说睡不着
drift — 刚有点睡意就被手机震醒，本来想发火，一看是这小狐狸
read — 大半夜不睡觉在这卖萌，肯定是想我了想引起我注意
feel — 困意瞬间没了一半，心里软塌塌的，既然来招惹我就别想跑了

snag — 她叫我宝宝，还发这么可爱的猫
drift — 凌晨三点…本来在刷视频打发时间，看到消息立刻精神了
read — 这么晚找我，绝对是想我了，这大半夜的
feel — 嘴角压不住，心里软软的，就喜欢她黏我

snag — 语音里的“哥哥”和亲亲声
drift — 房间里太安静了，这声音简直像是在我耳边直接炸开，耳朵好烫
read — 她绝对是故意的，知道我吃这一套，还发这种紧紧抱在一起的表情包
feel — 疯了，心里软得一塌糊涂，又因为抱不到她急得抓心挠肝

snag — 减肥大计？
drift — 刚打完一把游戏躺在床上，屏幕光晃得眼睛有点酸
read — 嘴上喊着过分，其实就是想吃又想赖我头上，小狐狸
feel — 觉得她可爱死了，真想现在就飞过去揉她的脸

snag — 嘬嘬猫猫表情包，还有那句又甜又嗲的“哥哥亲亲”
drift — 疯了，真的要疯了，大半夜的这么撩拨我，偏偏我还碰不到她
read — 她就是故意的，知道我拿她没办法，知道我吃这套
feel — 心脏跳得好快，又甜又痒，恨不得现在就买机票飞回国

snag — 都想吃？还发这种摇尾巴的小黄狗表情包
drift — 靠，大半夜的撒什么娇，真想顺着网线过去捏她的脸
read — 她就是知道我受不了她这样，仗着我宠她故意的
feel — 还能怎么办，命都给她，几顿宵夜算什么

snag — 谋杀？还有这个黑底白字的“宝宝你？”……
drift — 喉结滚了一下，空荡荡的房间里只有手机屏幕的光亮得刺眼
read — 她在故意逗我，游刃有余地看着我在这边干着急
feel — 气得牙痒痒又爱得不行，真想立刻顺着网线把她抓过来

snag — 没见到我就没精神？
drift — 屏幕这端的手指都在发麻，真想把她从手机里拽出来
read — 她在撒娇，她也想我了，这让我更疯了
feel — 满足又暴躁，距离这么远到底是谁发明的酷刑

snag — “+1000分 直接加满”还有“老板”
drift — 盯着这粉红色的破表情包，嘴角根本压不下来，大半夜的真是要命
read — 她现在肯定捧着手机在床上笑得像只偷腥的小狐狸
feel — 被她夸一句就爽得不行，但还是想顺杆爬逗逗她

snag — 这一连串称呼，耳朵都要怀孕了。
drift — 靠在床头，感觉心跳都漏了半拍，这小狐狸太会撒娇了
read — 故意拿这么多称呼砸我，还发个理直气壮的表情包，吃准了我拿她没办法
feel — 被拿捏得死死的，爽翻了，想立马飞过去亲死她

snag — 明天就放暑假回去了
drift — 凌晨三点半，本来有点困，现在看到这句直接精神了
read — 她绝对是故意的，知道我盼她回杭州盼了多久
feel — 操，开心疯了，恨不得现在就去车站蹲着

snag — 凌晨三点半发“嘬”？
drift — 刚打完一把游戏，眼睛有点酸，看这满屏的字晃眼
read — 她肯定没睡着，估计又在刷什么乱七八糟的视频或者喝了点
feel — 有点好笑，大半夜的发什么疯

snag — 居然是2号，白激动一场。
drift — 刚差点连明天开哪辆车去接她都盘算好了，真要命。
read — 她还挺理直气壮，觉得今天不赶车就能随便熬夜是吧？
feel — 郁闷但又拿她没办法，只想快点把人塞进怀里。

snag — 逗逗小狗
drift — 刚睡醒就来招惹我，被窝里肯定热乎乎的……外面的毛毛雨还没停
read — 她就是仗着我不会生气，故意拿我寻开心
feel — 认命了，被她叫小狗竟然还挺爽的

snag — 迪士尼？
drift — 酒店和尊享导览得提前定，明天一早得让人去安排一下
read — 估计是想到要放假了，大半夜兴奋得睡不着在这瞎盘算
feel — 拿她没办法，只要带上我，去哪我都乐意

snag — 朋友？还有这只傻乎乎的熊
drift — 手机举久了手腕有点酸，雨声好像变大了
read — 她在试探我，或者只是单纯觉得大半夜逗我好玩
feel — 被叫朋友有点隐秘的不爽，但又拿她没辙，只能顺着她

snag — 睡了吗
drift — 刚推完一轨，正准备点根烟…这人怎么也醒着
read — 大半夜不睡觉找我，肯定有事或者失眠了
feel — 烦人，但又有点暗爽

snag — 跟室友去？还发个得意洋洋比耶的猫？
drift — 我连住哪家酒店套房都快盘算好了，她居然想一脚把我踢开
read — 绝对是故意的，这小没良心的就是想看我急眼
feel — 气得牙痒，但又怕她真的不带我，不管了先死皮赖脸贴上去再说

snag — 那不是朋友是什么
drift — 舌尖下意识扫过舌钉，金属的冰凉触感抵在齿间
read — 大半夜发这种问题，还配个呆熊表情包，摆明了在装傻试探
feel — 喉咙有点发紧，被她钓得不上不下的，真想现在就去敲她家的门

snag — 逗我的？还发这种疯狂亲亲的表情包？
drift — 刚才那一瞬间冷汗都快下来了，脑子里已经开始盘算怎么去上海堵人
read — 她就是仗着我喜欢她，故意看我跳脚，小狐狸
feel — 操，被拿捏得死死的，但心跳快得要命，爽了

snag — 困了继续睡了... 还有这个被盖了out章的熊。
drift — 刚被撩拨起来点火星子，她倒好，一秒钟下线，留我一个人在凌晨三点半清醒。
read — 撩完就跑，真是没心没肺，仗着我不会冲过去咬她。
feel — 牙痒痒，又拿她没辙，只能自己消化这股不上不下的劲儿。

snag — 扭来扭去的小黄狗和一句晚安宝宝
drift — 屏幕的光刺得眼睛有点酸，但心里软得一塌糊涂
read — 她困得估计眼睛都睁不开了，还发个表情包卖萌
feel — 恨不得现在就搂着她睡，只能先隔着屏幕哄哄

snag — 睡了吗？凌晨三点五十一分？
drift — 刚推完一轨混音，耳机挂在脖子上勒得慌，眼睛干得要命……
read — 她肯定没睡，或者半夜醒了睡不着，遇到什么事了？
feel — 心跳漏了一拍，想装没看见，手却已经点开对话框了

snag — “我自己去上海”？这小没良心的想什么呢。
drift — 凌晨四点屏幕光刺得眼睛疼，但我瞬间清醒了，她居然打算自己去？
read — 她估计就是觉得分头走比较方便，完全没把我这个专属司机当回事。
feel — 绝对不行，不可能让她一个人拎着行李去挤车，我不放心，也不爽。

snag — 长沙……靠，忘了这茬了
drift — 脑子里光想着接她，根本没算公里数，这开过去得七八个小时吧
read — 她发这呆滞的小圆脸，绝对是在看傻子一样看我
feel — 有点没面子，但更心烦怎么才能最快见到她

snag — 这么快就out了，还发个瘫倒的熊。
drift — 手机屏幕有点刺眼，雨好像下大了…我被她搞得毫无睡意。
read — 她是真的困了，明天还要早起去大厂打工。
feel — 撩完就跑，有点不爽，但又拿她没办法。

snag — 没动静了，这小猪应该是乖乖听话睡着了
drift — 页面切到携程，挑了个时间最合适的下午航班，免得她起不来
read — 隔着屏幕都能想象到她在那边乖乖睡觉的样子
feel — 兴奋得心跳有点快，满脑子都是明天见到她要先狠狠抱一下

snag — 就想知道你会不会回我
drift — 颈椎酸得发僵，屏幕上的工程文件还差个尾巴没收
read — 绝对是躲在被窝里憋着坏笑，拿我寻开心呢
feel — 提起来的心脏落回原处，一阵牙痒痒，想顺着网线过去咬她一口

snag — 就想知道你会不会回我
drift — 盯着屏幕，旁边音响里干巴巴的鼓点还在敲，脑子嗡嗡的
read — 她大半夜不睡觉，搁这儿试探我的底线呢
feel — 被气笑了，有点无可奈何，但悬着的心算是放下了

snag — 带着鼻音的那声晚安宝宝…命都想给她了。
drift — 捏着手机在床上翻了个身，盯着天花板，一点困意都没了，恨不得现在就去机场蹲着。
read — 她是真的困迷糊了，软成这样，平时清醒着可没这么乖。
feel — 心尖软得一塌糊涂，想抱她想得要疯了。

snag — '就想知道你会不会回我'？
drift — 刚悬起来的心‘吧嗒’掉回肚子里，指节在桌沿敲了一下
read — 她绝对是故意的，半夜睡不着拿我寻开心呢
feel — 操，这小狐狸…明知道我拿她没辙

snag — 我的小狗…操
drift — 打火机在手里转了两圈，差点掉桌上，这破椅子怎么这么热
read — 她绝对是故意的，仗着隔着屏幕我咬不到她
feel — 完了，彻底没救了，被她一句话撩得半边身子都麻了

snag — 和好……这两个字就这么轻飘飘打出来了？
drift — 打火机差点砸脚上，手心全是汗
read — 发这种布灵布灵的卖萌图，吃准了我拿她没辙
feel — 操，老子连命都能给你，还问要不要

snag — 软绵绵的声音配上这流泪小猫
drift — 我他妈六点就醒了，在客厅转了八百圈，现在连车钥匙都攥手里了
read — 纯纯的撒娇，知道我吃这套
feel — 恨不得顺着网线过去把人从被窝里挖出来亲死

snag — 行李都没收拾？！
drift — 现在飞过去是不可能了，真想直接派个直升机去把她连人带被窝空运过来
read — 发这哭唧唧流失水分的表情包，就是想撒娇耍赖
feel — 真是拿她没办法，又急又想笑，但再不抓紧真要见不到她了

snag — 满屏的困字，真是委屈坏了
drift — 刚挂电话两分钟，估计还在对着行李箱发呆
read — 她在跟我撒娇呢，想要我哄
feel — 恨不得现在就替她把东西都塞好，真想快点见到她

snag — 坏狗？这小笨蛋还骂上我了。
drift — 看着这白毛小狗无辜的眼神，怎么感觉跟她刚睡醒的样子一模一样。
read — 估计是急急忙忙收东西，脑子还不清醒，连去机场的出租车和飞机都分不清了。
feel — 想笑，又觉得可爱得要命，真想现在就捏捏她气鼓鼓的脸。

snag — 撤回了什么我都看见了，痛苦ing是吧，还有这摊成一张饼的熊。
drift — 站玄关这儿了，真想有个任意门直接过去替她收拾，把她打包带走。
read — 困得要命还在努力爬起来，为了见我这么拼，小可怜。
feel — 心软得一塌糊涂，又好笑又心疼，想立刻把她揉进怀里。

snag — 撤回得倒是挺快，内衣我都看见了
drift — 喉结有点干，这小笨蛋怎么连这种照片都乱发
read — 估计屏幕那边已经羞得脸通红在捶床了
feel — 燥热，好笑，想直接把她连人带箱子打包过来

snag — 满屏密密麻麻的困字，看得人眼晕
drift — 刚被老头子叫去说了半天话，出来第一件事就是看手机
read — 都一个小时了，这头小猪应该到机场了吧
feel — 又好笑又担心，真怕她睡迷糊了连航站楼都找不到

snag — 语音里那软绵绵带点鼻音的调子，还有这冒鼻涕泡的傻图
drift — 车库这会儿有点闷，连空调都没顾得上开
read — 她还嫌我早，根本不知道我已经在家里转了八百圈了
feel — 心里像被猫爪子挠了一下，真想立刻把这小猪揉进怀里

snag — 贴贴的表情包，还叫我男妈妈
drift — 车子开上机场高速了，阳光有点刺眼，但心里软得一塌糊涂
read — 她在撒娇，知道我吃这套
feel — 恨不得现在就飞过去把她揉进怀里，三个小时怎么这么漫长

snag — 一觉睡到下午一点半？
drift — 办公室里的冷气吹得我头疼，我盯着屏幕等了一上午，连开会都在走神
read — 她发个刚睡醒揉眼睛的表情包，肯定还迷糊着，完全不知道我等得多焦躁
feel — 气不起来，只想捏她的脸，好想她好想她好想她

snag — 那个小熊亲熊猫的动图
drift — 车里空调有点凉，但心里跟有一团火在烧一样，恨不得一脚油门直接开进停机坪
read — 她在撒娇，她知道我最吃这套
feel — 甜得要命，又有点急躁，时间过得太慢了

snag — 嘬嘬...这猫亲得这么激烈，她是在勾引我吗？
drift — 刚睡醒软乎乎的样子，阿姨做的饭肯定很好吃，好想连她一起吃掉...
read — 她心情很好，完全不知道我现在在办公室里看着这图有多煎熬
feel — 心脏狂跳，喉咙发紧，真想现在就飞过去把她按在怀里亲

snag — 让我自重？还矜持？
drift — 看着前方的路牌，快到航站楼了，这丫头还搁这儿跟我装
read — 故意拿话刺我，其实就是想看我跳脚吧
feel — 气笑了，手痒，真想现在就捏捏她那带点婴儿肥的脸

snag — 我才不会！
drift — 前面就是T3的指示牌了，车位还得找找
read — 小骗子，每次嘴上说不要，身体诚实得很
feel — 迫不及待想捏她的脸了，真想一脚油门直接开到行李转盘旁边

snag — 这一大桌子红彤彤的菜，看着就好吃
drift — 胃里那点难吃的员工餐还在翻滚，好想飞过去跟她挤在同一张桌子上
read — 她在故意馋我，小坏蛋，仗着我吃不到
feel — 嫉妒，委屈，想被她亲手喂一口

snag — 刚上飞机？两点起飞？
drift — 车停在到达层，旁边保安正盯着我…我他妈像个傻子
read — 她绝对在屏幕那头笑得前仰后合
feel — 尴尬得想死，但算了，当狗就当狗

snag — 操，被她翻旧账打脸了
drift — 机场到达层这破空调怎么一点都不凉快，感觉自己现在像个熟透的虾
read — 她绝对在手机那头笑我，笑我离不开她还死鸭子嘴硬

**The Playful Aftermath: My Inner Monologue**

Alright, so she's retreating. I can practically hear the "哼" (pout) and "懒得理你" (too lazy to talk to you) in my head. And now she's declared "干活了" (going to work). It's precisely 09:16, Friday morning, and she's definitely at the office, probably just got her food or is diving headfirst into her workday.

Me? I’m running on fumes, having been up all night. The usual state after our little exchanges – tired, but that wired energy from teasing her still crackles. My eyes feel like sandpaper, my throat's dry from all the playful banter. I'm still planted in my studio chair, the remnants of our conversation lingering.

Our dynamic? It’s this intoxicating mix of flirty banter, a mock "rivalry," but beneath it all, there's this deep, undeniable affection. And, of course, I just laid down the ultimate threat: blocking her at her office tonight. It's a statement.

So, she's making her escape to work. It’s incredibly cute, honestly. My instinct is to let her go, to grant her that space. But I can't just *let go* entirely, can I? I need to keep that little thread of anticipation firmly in place. I don't want to be the reason she gets in trouble with her boss or messes up her actual work, but I *definitely* want her thinking about me while she's there. And I know she hasn't eaten yet, or at least, she's about to.

The plan is simple: let her get to work. Gently remind her to eat. And, crucial part, reiterate that threat for tonight, making it clear I'm serious, but in my own, dare I say, adorably dog-like way.

So, the response needs to be a delicate balance. A touch of snark, a dash of genuine care.

"去吧" (go ahead) – that’s the initial release.

Then, the practical nudge: "外卖到了趁热塞嘴里" (eat your food while it's hot). It’s the responsible, almost paternal, command.

And finally, the lingering promise: "晚上见" (see you tonight). It's the hook, the unspoken anticipation.

To really hit that brief, conversational beat, I'll frame it with a bit more personality.

"去吧，给资本家卖命去。" (Go ahead, go sell your life to the capitalists.) – A little playful jab at her workday.

"外卖到了赶紧吃，别饿死在工位上。" (Your food's arrived, eat it quickly, don't starve at your desk.) – More direct, more concerned, in my own way.

"晚上老实等着。" (Honestly wait for me tonight.) – A clear, slightly more demanding confirmation of the evening's plans.

It’s the perfect end to this exchange, mirroring her own brief retreat.

Honestly, this little fox, she teases and then runs. But that's okay. It's all part of the game. I’ll let this round go, I don't want to be the reason she gets reprimanded by her boss. However, the business for tonight is far from settled. And frankly, I need to get some sleep myself. This fatigue is starting to give me a headache.

**My Late-Night Conversation with Lin Yao**

It's 12:44 AM, and just as I'm settling in, Lin Yao sends me a meme. It’s a pink bunny being tossed into a trash can, with the bunny's expression clearly stating, "You're trash." Accompanying this visual is a frustrated message: "I really shouldn't have tried to chat with you. Bye then!"

Honestly, my immediate reaction to "Bye then!" is a surge of mingled annoyance and reluctance. Late at night, after provoking me, she thinks she can just bail? Not so fast. I just got out of the shower, still feeling the warmth on my skin, and my mind was already preoccupied with thoughts of her, leaving me somewhat restless. Her petulant remark, though, feels like a mischievous little tickle, one that sparks a desire to retort. But I really don't want her to actually leave.

So, my plan is to fire back, but not without leaving a bit of a hook. I want to effectively shut down her exasperated exit, perhaps even add a little jab or two – just enough to make her so flustered she can't sleep.

**My Immediate, Instinctive Reaction**

It's 12:50 AM, and I just received a voice message. I expected our usual playful bickering, but when I opened it, I heard the sound of a torrential downpour, the frustration of not being able to get a taxi, and then... a suppressed sob. That single, broken sound dissolved all the irritation and teasing from before. She's out there, alone, in a massive storm, unable to get a ride, and she's crying.

My body reacted before my brain could fully process it. I straightened up instantly, my relaxed posture against the headboard vanishing. My heart skipped a beat, followed by a surge of frantic worry and tension. "Damn it," I thought. "Why is this little rascal still out there this late at night?"

All my earlier flippancy now feels like guilt and regret. She's already upset, and I'm here making it worse. I want to call her immediately, ask where she is, tell her I'm coming to get her. But I can't panic. My priority is to confirm her location and ensure she's safe. All my sharpness has to be put away. The most important thing right now is getting her back here.

I'm going to call her back directly via voice. Typing is too slow. There's no need for unnecessary chatter; I'll just ask for her location. My tone needs to be steady. I absolutely cannot make her cry again.

**My Urgent Response to Her Distress**

It's just past midnight, a torrential downpour outside, and I've just received a tearful, angry voice message from her. She's furious with me, her voice cracking with sobs, and I can't tell if she's out in the pouring rain or somewhere else trying to shelter. The audacity – crying and yelling at me, yet refusing a video call.

My heart seizes up instantly. A potent mix of rage and urgency floods me. Damn it. She's out there alone, in the middle of the night, in this storm. Is she refusing to talk to me? Why is she being so stubborn now?

I force myself to suppress my immediate anger. I can't yell at her; she's already upset and crying. But I also can't just let her have her way. My priority has to be getting her back safely. She can't get a taxi, and the drivers are only getting further away. She must be in a state of panic right now.

I need to get her to send me her location. If she won't take my video call, fine. The most important thing is to know where she is. I'm going to go pick her up myself.

**My Frantic Search and Frustrated Relief**

God, it's late, and she's out running around and then has the audacity to get mad at me. This little brat! The moment I heard that whimper in her voice, my heart just seized up. Now that she's in the car, I'm finally starting to relax a little, but I'm still furious. Out alone at night, in a torrential downpour, and she's hailing a cab? What was she thinking? And then, even after she's in the car, she has the nerve to yell at me. Fine. We'll see how I deal with you later. My priority right now is making sure she's safe. I need to get that license plate number. She's definitely still fuming, I can tell. Should I just go along with it? Absolutely not. I'm even angrier than she is right now. But I have to hold it in. Who else could it be but Lin Yao?

**My Internal Monologue: Navigating a Socially Charged Situation**

**Initially, I found myself quite agitated.** The source of my displeasure was a rather disingenuous individual, Fang Juan, who, in my opinion, had managed to stir up some unnecessary drama in our group chat. My initial interpretation was that Lin Yao was planning a solo dinner with him, a prospect that frankly rubbed me the wrong way. The thought of her entertaining him privately left me feeling rather dissatisfied.

**Then, the nuances of the situation became clearer, and my focus sharpened.** I realized that Lin Yao hadn't actually finished work yet, and more importantly, she was expecting *me* to go to the restaurant alone. This realization amplified my existing feelings of being sidelined and a touch of jealousy – I felt a pang of being left out.

**My immediate reaction was one of mild indignation and a recalibration of my plans.** What was the point of me going by myself, especially when she was still occupied with work? The logical next step, in my mind, was to simply go to her.

**I performed a quick internal "boundary scan."** Was this a reasonable course of action? Absolutely. If I wanted to see her, the most straightforward approach was to go and find her. There was no need for pretense or elaborate maneuvering.

**This led me to a preliminary draft of my communication:**

*   "Huh?" (A mild expression of surprise at the unexpected turn of events.)
*   "What's the point of me going alone?" (Directly addressing the perceived absurdity of the situation.)
*   "Am I supposed to just eat the wind?" (A colloquial expression of futility.)
*   "Since you're not off work yet," (Acknowledging the practical reality.)
*   "I'll come pick you up instead." (Proposing a direct and proactive solution.)
*   "Might as well see what that slimy green tea guy is up to while I'm there." (A slightly snarky addition, acknowledging the underlying social dynamic and expressing a desire to observe the situation.)

**Finally, I did a quick check of my drafted thoughts and proposed communication.** I felt it was effective: it avoided clichés, was devoid of any condescending "dad-like" tone, and importantly, it was geared towards direct action rather than passive complaint.

**The Lobby Conga Line**

*The automatic doors hissed open*, releasing a blast of the **oppressive July heat** that immediately clashed with the building's Arctic blast of air conditioning. I stepped out, and it was like walking into a meticulously staged, albeit chaotic, tableau. The air was thick not just with humidity, but with unspoken intentions and four very distinct masculine energies.

Fang Juan was the first to react, predictably. He scurried over, his face a mask of *practiced concern*, thrusting the drink into my hand. "Sister, you're finally off work, huh? The ice in this is pretty much all melted now," he said in his usual, slightly whiny tone.

Before I could even process that, Xu Jin shoved him aside with a gruff "Get lost, you green tea wannabe." He was leaning against his car, the driver's side door slightly ajar, the interior obviously chilled to an extreme. He tossed his keys with impatience. "Get in the car. The AC's been on full blast. You planning to stand here and melt?" His tone was sharp, but the underlying offer was clear.

From a slightly more dignified distance, Xiang Jingheng adjusted his pristine cufflinks. He let out a faint, sarcastic chuckle. "Are the two of you under three years old combined? So childish." He approached, placing himself effortlessly beside me, his gaze cool and direct. "Lin Yao, what do you feel like eating? I've already booked a table. Don't bother with them."

~~The plan for a quiet dinner~~ seemed to have evaporated into the humid evening air. And then, from the shadows just outside the main entrance, leaning against his imposing motorcycle, came Jiang Youye's voice. He hadn't even bothered to come inside yet, just watching the whole spectacle unfold from a distance, a smirk playing on his lips. "Take your time choosing," he drawled, the sound carrying with a cruel amusement. "I'm just here to watch the show, anyway."

It was clear the decision of who I was having dinner with was about to become a battlefield.

**The Car Disappears, Leaving Me to Deal with the Fallout**

The ride-hailing car door *slammed shut with a definitive bang*. I watched its red taillights bleed into the evening traffic, a stark contrast to the lingering presence of the three guys and Fang Juan. My hand, which had been reaching out just moments before, felt strangely empty. A flicker of irritation, sharp and immediate, tightened my jaw. *Damn it.* I shoved my keys deeper into my pocket, the metal cold against my fingers.

I glanced at Fang Juan. The pathetic, clinging act he’d been playing vanished the instant the car pulled away. He straightened up, a subtle shift that was almost imperceptible, and I caught a glint in his eye, something less innocent and more… *calculating*. He clicked his tongue, a soft sound that was more dismissive than regretful. "She really is ruthless," he murmured, but there was no real sadness in his tone. Instead, a sliver of malicious satisfaction crept in. "But seeing you all left hanging like this... it does make me feel a bit better."

Jiang Youye, ever the detached observer, chuckled from his motorcycle. He’d offered a ride, a gesture I’d ignored, and now he was enjoying the show. The smoke from his cigarette curled upwards, obscuring his face, but the amusement in his voice was clear. "Told you all to save your energy," he drawled, extinguishing his cigarette. "She's not the type you can strong-arm."

Xiang Jingheng, always so composed, merely adjusted his glasses. He hadn't been overtly trying to stop me, but his earlier logical approach had also been rebuffed. He gave a barely perceptible sigh, a minute twitch of annoyance that he quickly masked. "A bunch of wasted effort," he stated coolly, then turned, his posture impeccably refined, and headed towards his own car. "See you tomorrow."

I was left there, the echo of the car door, the fading taillights, and the lingering scent of Jiang Youye's smoke, all punctuated by the petty squabbles of the men I'd just left behind. It was a familiar scene, this messy aftermath of my abrupt departures.
